description: Where each H5P library shows a correct or incorrect answer (UD-003). `correct`/`incorrect`: the element that gets the label (src/feedbackPrefixes.js); pick one whose children the library does not count or select by position (`:first-child`); an entry may name one state only. `prefixOn`: the element whose pseudo-element shows the visible prefix, when it differs (dist/hvl-feedback-prefixes.css); pick one whose pseudo-element the library does not use and whose size it does not fix; a selector list is fine. `prefixPseudo`: `after` draws the prefix as `::after` instead of `::before`. `prefixOn: "label"`: the library uses the pseudo-elements, so the script shows its label as text instead (needs ownIcon). `ownIcon`: the library already draws a ✓/✗ icon for the state, so the visible prefix is the label only. A target inside a radio, checkbox, option or button named by aria-label also gets the label in front of that name.

targets.library: H5P.MultiChoice 1.16 solution (a filled or empty radio or checkbox, not a ✓/✗)
H5P.TrueFalse 1.8 (::before is the radio, ::after the ✓/✗ box)
H5P.MarkTheWords 1.11 solution (a missed word: dashed border, no icon)
H5P.SingleChoiceSet 1.11 chosen alternative (its ✓/✗ is .h5p-sc-status; the label goes into the answer's first paragraph, which SingleChoiceSet styles as :first-child)
H5P.SingleChoiceSet 1.11 revealed alternatives the learner did not choose (no icon)
H5P.Summary 1.10 (li::before is the ✓/✗; a wrong claim is named by aria-label)
H5P.MultiMediaChoice 0.3 (::before is the ✓/✗ badge; the option is named by aria-label)
H5P.ImageHotspotQuestion 1.8 (the click mark is a fixed 32 px circle whose ::before is the ✓/✗; the image clips it, so the label is the image's ::after beside it)
